**Question.** Which range will hold the total of U.S. clade I mpox cases in the latest CDC situation summary published before 1 January 2027? A figure given as "more than X" counts as X+1.

**Starting point.** The CDC page, updated 16 November 2026, says "more than 200" laboratory-confirmed clade I cases since November 2024, in at least 31 states plus Puerto Rico. That is 201 today, in the lowest range, so the answer turns on how many more revisions appear and how fast the count climbs.

**Recent evidence.**
- The count is accelerating: 14 cases on 20 March (Missouri health department), 23 in late May (Medical Daily, 11 June), 50 by 31 July (PAHO report, 28 August), more than 90 on 14 October (CDC figure cited by Medical Daily, 31 October) and more than 200 by 16 November. The last step is about 110 cases in 33 days, roughly 23 a week, against about 4 a week from August to mid-October.
- CDC now describes a "likely transition to sustained clade Ib transmission", with presumed domestic spread in 16 jurisdictions; Colorado (18 November) and Alaska (20 November) have just reported their first cases.
- The page has been revised every one to three weeks. Federal funding runs out on 11 December, and the holidays may make a mid-December revision the last of the year.

**Combining.** A steady 25-30 cases a week puts the count near 305-355 by 14-21 December. If the recent doubling about every three weeks continues, it passes 400 by mid-December. If growth slows, or the last revision comes in early December, it lands at 250-295. The two lowest ranges need the page to go almost unrevised for six weeks. The main ways this could be wrong: the October-November jump may include a backlog of newly typed cases, which would overstate the pace, and CDC may round more coarsely as the number grows.

**Forecast.** Under 210: 4%; 210-245: 5%; 246-295: 19%; 296-370: 34%; Greater than 370: 38%.
